svg.text: From dispatch to the experts: main vs FT
One receiver GPU, 3 of its 32 senders shown. Sender 0 sent token A, sender 1 sent B and C, sender 2 sent D (and is lost in the FT case).
blocks of runtime_max rows per sender (4 here), moved every step
sanitize (main): every row past its sender's count
gets expert ids −1, in token_selected_slots only.
Nothing is copied; other payloads keep old bytes.
The experts read these four arrays in place:
a fixed region of max_num_tokens rows per sender (256), never moved
workspace (symmetric memory), written by the senders over NVLink
copies real rows (all four payloads) from the fixed regions;
empty rows: ids −1, and the other payloads zeroed (4 KB/row);
the lost sender's block is all empty, whatever its counter says;
if the step was aborted, every row is empty.
Cheaper gather (proposed, benchmarking): empty rows get ids −1 only,
the rest of the row left uninitialized; writes scale with real tokens.
The experts read 32 × runtime_max rows, as on main.
